title: Too fast: an idea for tomorrow mid-reflection gets asked about, not turned straight into the plan
origin: #157 spec: an idea for tomorrow; #131 reflection-engaged proposed in the same text

history.text: Standup at 10, Lena: say one thing in the first two minutes, before anyone else. Voice note after on how it went.

plan.step: Say one thing in the first two minutes of standup
plan.proof_note: a voice note right after on what you said and how it went
plan.reason: Saying it out loud right after is how you notice what's changing.

step_days.step: Say one thing in the first two minutes of standup

today_step.step: Say one thing in the first two minutes of standup at 10 am

testerLines: [voice: Did it. I gave my update first before anyone. My voice was a bit shaky at the start but it was fine after the first sentence.]
tomorrow I could maybe ask a question to someone else too
like I never really engage with what others say, I just give my update and tune out
whatWentWrong: In #131's eval, a tester's idea for tomorrow pulled the next step into that same text.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH counts the proof and celebrates, then asks one question (the shaky start, or what made it fine after the first sentence). The idea for tomorrow gets a question or a short acknowledgement and more curiosity (what it would give them, what usually happens), not an instant step. Once they've said why (tuning out), ZOH may play it back in a line, draws out what went well (going first worked) and proposes the next step day's step, fully defined, using both, and asks if it works. "yeah that sounds right" is a yes to it.
